activity_context.topic_title: Estimating Derivatives Using a Forward Difference Quotient

feedback.problem:
A function $g(x)$ has values according to the table below:

| $x$ | $-2$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $g(x)$ | $20.4$ | $18.6$ | $16.5$ | $14.4$ | $12.3$ | $10.8$ |

Approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=2$ using a forward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

${g}^{′}(2)≈$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x+h)-g(x)}{h}
$$

at the point $x=2.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=2.$ This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(2) & ≈\frac{g(2+2)-g(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{g(4)-g(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{14.4-16.5}{2} \\  & =\frac{-2.1}{2} \\  & =-1.05.\end{aligned}
$$
